headline: Open-weight models (DeepSeek-R1, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B) have narrowed the raw coding benchmark gap on SWE-bench and LiveCodeBench, but proprietary frontier agents (Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet) maintain a decisive lead in multi-turn agentic execution and complex repository repair.

key_findings.finding: On SWE-bench Verified, Claude 3.5 Sonnet leads at 49.0%–53.7%, while DeepSeek-R1 reaches ~49.2% and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B achieves 35.2%–40.0%, demonstrating that open-weight models have reached frontier parity in single-turn reasoning but still lag in unassisted autonomous agent loops.
On out-of-distribution evaluation suites like LiveCodeBench, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B and DeepSeek-V3 reach ~37.6%–40.5% Pass@1, competitive with GPT-4o but behind Claude 3.5 Sonnet (41.4%–51.1%).

On the Aider Polyglot Benchmark, Claude 3.5 Sonnet remains the top-performing model for multi-file editing stability, with Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct establishing itself as the leading open-weight alternative.

claims.text: Claude 3.5 Sonnet achieves 49.0% to 53.7% resolution rate on SWE-bench Verified across standard and specialized agentic scaffoldings.

evidence.snippet: Claude 3.5 Sonnet scored 49.0% with basic scaffolding and 53.7% with specialized agentic harnesses on SWE-bench Verified.

claims.text: DeepSeek-R1 achieves approximately 49.2% resolution rate on SWE-bench Verified, matching proprietary frontier reasoning performance.

evidence.snippet: DeepSeek-R1 scored ~49.2% on SWE-bench Verified, demonstrating state-of-the-art open-weights reasoning capability.

claims.text: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct achieves 35.2% to 40.0% on SWE-bench Verified, outperforming older closed models (like GPT-4o-mini) and establishing a strong baseline for dense open weights.

evidence.snippet: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct scored ~35.2% on SWE-bench Verified base scaffold and higher with multi-turn agents like Aider and SWE-agent.

claims.text: On LiveCodeBench Pass@1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet scores between 41.4% and 51.1%, leading open-weight dense models on unseen competitive programming problems.

evidence.snippet: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (2024-10-22) achieves ~41.4% - 51.1% on LiveCodeBench Pass@1 depending on time slice and split.

claims.text: DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct achieve 37.6% to 40.5% Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench, showing parity with GPT-4o but remaining slightly behind Claude 3.5 Sonnet.

evidence.snippet: DeepSeek-V3 achieves ~38.6% - 40.5% and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct achieves ~37.6% - 40.0% on LiveCodeBench Pass@1.

claims.text: On the Aider polyglot code editing benchmark, Claude 3.5 Sonnet ranks as the top commercial model for complex multi-file diff generation and instruction adherence.

evidence.snippet: Claude 3.5 Sonnet frequently tops the Aider leaderboard and is considered the gold standard for agentic coding in real-world repo scenarios.

claims.text: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct is recognized on the Aider benchmark as the highest-ranking sub-40B open-weights model, capable of matching proprietary models like GPT-4o-mini in edit format compliance.

evidence.snippet: Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B consistently scores high on the Aider benchmark, matching or outperforming closed models like GPT-4o-mini.

claims.text: The performance trajectory heading into 2026 suggests open-weight models compress the performance lag behind proprietary models to 3 to 6 months on benchmark tasks, but proprietary agents maintain an advantage in integrated tool calling and long-horizon autonomy.

evidence.snippet: Open-weight models on SWE-bench improved from <10% in early 2024 (DeepSeek-Coder-1.3B/33B) to nearly 50% by early 2025 (DeepSeek-R1).
Rapid iteration cycles in open weights have narrowed the gap on static coding benchmarks significantly within a 12-month window.

writing_context.text: SWE-bench Verified filters out unsolvable or ambiguous tasks from SWE-bench Full to reduce scoring noise. LiveCodeBench collects problems continuously to prevent train-set contamination.
writing_context.use: Note benchmark methodologies when comparing raw resolution percentages.
